title: The Midnight Garden
premise: Emrys Thornbury carves bones into charms for the dying in a valley walled off by an ancient covenant, where magic cannot enter and the dead speak only to him. When the old gods resume answering prayers, the covenant begins to crack, and Emrys learns the valley was never a sanctuary but a prison for a god the founders murdered to survive a famine. To escape the unraveling country, he must find the Door of Ash, guarded by the descendants of those founders, and decide whether justice means freeing the imprisoned god — even if doing so erases every memory the valley's people have of their dead. In the end, Emrys opens the door, lets the god pass, and carries the valley's memories out as the last bone-carver, alone but unbound.
about_author: Sebastian Joubert is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing folk charms in rural collections before turning to fiction. They write quiet, bone-deep fantasy about grief, bargains, and the people history forgot to bury.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgot
chapters.summary: Emrys carves a memorial bone for a drowned child, hearing the dead murmur through the marrow. His neighbor Maren begs him to pray at the old shrine, but prayers have been useless for a century. Emrys refuses, fearing what listening costs him. Emotional beat: the loneliness of being the valley's only mourner who truly hears.

chapters.title: A Prayer Answered
chapters.summary: Maren's prayer is answered — a miracle of healing at the ruined shrine — and the valley erupts in terrified joy. Emrys, in his POV, hears the dead go silent for the first time in his life, as if something vast has drawn a breath. Emotional beat: hope shadowed by dread.

chapters.title: What the Bones Remember
chapters.summary: Emrys examines an heirloom bone charm that has begun to bleed warmth. The dead whisper fragments: a famine, a bargain, a god bound beneath the shrine. POV Emrys. Emotional beat: the sickening realization his whole life sits atop a crime.

chapters.title: The Covenant's Edge
chapters.summary: Emrys walks to the valley's border stones and finds the invisible wall flickering — a bird crosses where nothing should. A stranger, Ilsa Vane, waits outside, claiming to be a door-seeker hunting the Door of Ash. POV alternates to Ilsa. Emotional beat: first contact with a wider, lawless world.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: Emrys breaks into the moot-hall archive and finds the founders' ledger: nine names, a famine winter, and a ritual of binding written in bone-dust. His own family name is among the nine. POV Emrys. Emotional beat: inheritance as guilt.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ilsa smuggles herself inside as the covenant weakens. She offers Emrys a partnership: she knows the Door's location; he alone can open it, because it answers only to a founder's blood. POV Ilsa, revealing her own debt to a god who answered her sister's dying prayer. Emotional beat: wary alliance.

chapters.title: The Moot of Nine
chapters.summary: The valley council, descendants of the founders, convenes in panic as crops fail and the border thins. Elder Coram Thornbury, Emrys's uncle, demands renewed sacrifices to keep the god bound. POV Emrys. Emotional beat: the machinery of survival choosing cruelty.

chapters.title: First Blood at the Shrine
chapters.summary: Coram's faction sacrifices livestock, then threatens a person. Emrys intervenes and publicly accuses the founders of murder, splitting the valley. The dead begin screaming through every bone in his workshop. POV Emrys. Emotional beat: the cost of speaking truth.

chapters.title: The God Below
chapters.summary: Emrys descends into the shrine's hollow and meets the bound god — not a monster but a starved, patient presence that shows him the famine winter from its own eyes. It does not ask for freedom; it asks to be remembered. POV Emrys. Emotional beat: pity for the imprisoned.

chapters.title: Maren's Choice
chapters.summary: Maren, whose healing miracle was the god leaking through, joins Emrys but hides that her daughter is the next chosen sacrifice. POV Maren. Emotional beat: a mother's quiet, terrible arithmetic.

chapters.title: Coram's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Coram confronts Emrys with the family secret: their line volunteered for the binding to spare their own children. He believes the covenant is mercy, not murder. POV Coram. Emotional beat: antagonist humanized; justice revealed as perspective.

chapters.title: The Road of Ash
chapters.summary: Emrys, Ilsa, and Maren slip past the failing border and travel the dead lands outside, where the old gods' return has caused chaos — answered prayers curdling into fanaticism. POV Ilsa. Emotional beat: the outside world is no freer than the valley.

chapters.title: The Door-Seekers
chapters.summary: The trio reaches a lawless town of door-seekers who hunt thresholds between dying countries. Their leader recognizes Ilsa's debt-mark and demands she trade Emrys's blood for passage. POV Ilsa. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against survival.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Toll
chapters.summary: Ilsa considers selling Emrys; instead she burns her debt-mark, severing herself from her god's protection. They fight free of the town, Maren wounded. POV Ilsa. Emotional beat: justice chosen over safety, at personal ruin.

chapters.title: The Hollow Country
chapters.summary: They cross a region erased from all maps — the valley's original lands, unmade when the god was bound. Emrys hears the dead of the famine here, thousands strong, and nearly drowns in their grief. POV Emrys. Emotional beat: the true scale of the founders' crime.

chapters.title: Maren's Confession
chapters.summary: Maren admits her daughter has been marked for sacrifice; the moot moved the rite forward. She begs Emrys to abandon the Door and save her child. POV Maren. Emotional beat: the personal colliding with the cosmic.

chapters.title: The Door of Ash
chapters.summary: They find the Door — a threshold of grey bone in the hollow country — and learn the truth: opening it frees the god but unbinds the covenant, and the valley will be unmade like these lands unless the dead are carried out in living memory. POV Emrys. Emotional beat: the price made explicit.

chapters.title: The Sacrifice Interrupted
chapters.summary: Emrys races back alone as Coram begins the rite with Maren's daughter. He offers his own founder's blood instead, and the god accepts — but demands to be carried out through him, memory by memory. POV Emrys. Emotional beat: substitution, surrender.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: The god rises; the covenant shatters; the valley begins to dissolve. Coram, broken, helps Emrys anchor the people rather than resist. The dead of two centuries pass through Emrys as he carves their names into his own bones. POV Emrys. Emotional beat: climax — grief transmuted into bearing witness.

chapters.title: Exodus Through the Door
chapters.summary: The valley's people walk the Road of Ash toward the Door, guided by Ilsa and Maren, while the freed god passes over them like weather — neither thanked nor feared. POV Ilsa. Emotional beat: a nation walking out of erasure.

chapters.title: What the Door Keeps
chapters.summary: At the threshold, the god offers Emrys rest among the dead he carries. He refuses: someone must remember on the living side. The people pass through; the Door closes on the hollow country forever. POV Emrys. Emotional beat: choosing the burden of memory.

chapters.title: The Last Bone-Carver
chapters.summary: On the far side, the survivors build anew. Emrys, now hearing only silence where the dead were, opens a workshop and begins carving their names into a garden of bone-white stone. Maren's daughter brings him flowers. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — memory as the only justice that outlasts the law.
